nodes.title: Quality management system for providers of high-risk AI systems
nodes.statement: European harmonised standard specifying quality management system requirements for providers of high-risk AI systems, developed by CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 under the Commission's standardisation request supporting Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

nodes.title: Data and data governance
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of models shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet quality criteria. Data governance and management practices shall address design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations such as annotation, labelling, cleaning and aggregation, formulation of assumptions, assessment of availability quantity and suitability, and examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination. Data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Technical documentation
nodes.statement: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up to date. It shall demonstrate that the system complies with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2 and provide national competent authorities and notified bodies with the information necessary to assess that compliance. It shall contain, as a minimum, the elements set out in Annex IV.

nodes.title: Record-keeping
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system. Logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for identifying situations that may result in the system presenting a risk or undergoing a substantial modification, facilitating post-market monitoring, and monitoring the operation of the system.

nodes.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed so that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately. They shall be accompanied by instructions for use containing concise, complete, correct and clear information, including the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance, the level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, any known or foreseeable circumstances which may lead to risks to health, safety or fundamental rights, and the human oversight measures in place.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Human oversight
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use. Oversight shall aim to prevent or minimise risks to health, safety or fundamental rights. Persons assigned oversight shall be enabled to understand the system's capacities and limitations, remain aware of automation bias, correctly interpret output, decide not to use the system or to disregard, override or reverse its output, and intervene or interrupt operation through a stop button or similar procedure.

nodes.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and to perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle. Levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics shall be declared in the instructions for use. Systems shall be resilient against errors, faults and inconsistencies, and against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities, including data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion and confidentiality attacks.

nodes.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
nodes.statement: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall ensure their systems comply with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2, indicate their identity and contact details on the system or its packaging, operate a quality management system, keep the documentation required by Article 18, keep the automatically generated logs required by Article 19, ensure the system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment before being placed on the market, draw up an EU declaration of conformity, affix the CE marking, comply with registration obligations, take necessary corrective actions, and demonstrate conformity on request of a national competent authority.

nodes.title: Quality management system
nodes.statement: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put a quality management system in place that ensures compliance with this Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in written policies, procedures and instructions. It shall include a strategy for regulatory compliance, procedures for design, design control and verification, development, quality control and quality assurance, examination, test and validation procedures, technical specifications, systems and procedures for data management, the risk management system of Article 9, post-market monitoring, incident reporting procedures, handling of communication with authorities, record keeping, resource management and an accountability framework.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Documentation keeping
nodes.statement: Providers shall keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities, for a period ending ten years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service, the technical documentation, the documentation concerning the quality management system, the documentation concerning changes approved by notified bodies, the decisions and other documents issued by notified bodies, and the EU declaration of conformity.

nodes.title: Automatically generated logs
nodes.statement: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by their systems, to the extent those logs are under their control. The logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
nodes.statement: Providers which consider or have reason to consider that a high-risk AI system they have placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with this Regulation shall immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring it into conformity, to withdraw it, to disable it, or to recall it, and shall inform the distributors, deployers, authorised representative and importers accordingly.

nodes.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
nodes.statement: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use, assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority as well as the necessary support, ensure input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose where they exercise control over it, monitor the operation of the system, and keep the automatically generated logs for at least six months where those logs are under their control.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
nodes.statement: Before deploying certain high-risk AI systems, deployers that are bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, or deployers of systems used for creditworthiness evaluation or for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance, shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that use of the system may produce, covering the deployer's processes, the period and frequency of intended use, the categories of natural persons likely to be affected, the specific risks of harm, the human oversight measures, and the measures to be taken if risks materialise.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Harmonised standards and standardisation deliverables
nodes.statement: High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models which are in conformity with harmonised standards, or parts thereof, the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union, shall be presumed to be in conformity with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2, or as applicable the obligations of Chapter V Sections 2 and 3, to the extent those standards cover those requirements or obligations.

nodes.title: Conformity assessment
nodes.statement: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service, the provider shall ensure the system undergoes the applicable conformity assessment procedure, either based on internal control or involving a notified body, depending on the category of system and whether harmonised standards have been applied. A new conformity assessment is required whenever the system is substantially modified.

nodes.title: Registration
nodes.statement: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.

nodes.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
nodes.statement: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed so that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed person. Providers of systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems shall inform the persons exposed to them.

nodes.title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
nodes.statement: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall draw up and keep up to date the technical documentation of the model including its training and testing process and evaluation results, make information and documentation available to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the model, put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights, and draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training the model.

nodes.title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
nodes.statement: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing with a view to identifying and mitigating systemic risk, assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, keep track of, document and report without undue delay serious incidents and possible corrective measures to the AI Office and relevant national competent authorities, and ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.

nodes.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
nodes.statement: An AI system is classified as high-risk where it is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I and is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment. In addition, AI systems referred to in Annex III are classified as high-risk, covering areas including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education and vocational training, employment, workers management and access to self-employment, access to essential private and public services, law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control, and administration of justice and democratic processes.

nodes.title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan
nodes.statement: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system. The system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data, which may be provided by deployers or collected through other sources, on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime, and allow the provider to evaluate continuous compliance with the requirements of Chapter III Section 2.

nodes.title: Reporting of serious incidents
nodes.statement: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred, immediately after the provider has established a causal link between the AI system and the serious incident or the reasonable likelihood of such a link, and in any event not later than 15 days after becoming aware of the serious incident.

nodes.title: Risk management system
nodes.statement: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system that runs as a continuous iterative process across the entire lifecycle of the system, requiring regular systematic review and updating. It shall identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights, estimate risks arising from intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse, and adopt targeted risk management measures. Residual risk must be judged acceptable. High-risk systems shall be tested to identify the most appropriate risk management measures.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Continual improvement
nodes.statement: The organisation continually improves the suitability adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system.

nodes.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
nodes.statement: When a nonconformity occurs the organisation reacts to it evaluates the need for action to eliminate its causes implements action and reviews effectiveness.

nodes.title: Understanding the organization and its context
nodes.statement: The organisation determines external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcomes of the information security management system.

nodes.title: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
nodes.statement: The organisation determines interested parties relevant to the ISMS and their relevant requirements including legal and regulatory requirements.

nodes.title: Determining the scope of the information security management system
nodes.statement: The boundaries and applicability of the ISMS are determined and documented.

nodes.title: Information security management system
nodes.statement: The organisation establishes implements maintains and continually improves an ISMS including the processes needed and their interactions.

nodes.title: Leadership and commitment
nodes.statement: Top management demonstrates leadership and commitment with respect to the information security management system.

nodes.title: Policy
nodes.statement: Top management establishes an information security policy appropriate to the purpose of the organisation that includes objectives and a commitment to continual improvement.

nodes.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
nodes.statement: Top management ensures that responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities - general
nodes.statement: When planning the ISMS the organisation considers the issues and requirements identified and determines the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed.

nodes.title: Information security risk assessment
nodes.statement: The organisation defines and applies an information security risk assessment process that establishes risk criteria identifies analyses and evaluates risks and produces consistent valid and comparable results.

nodes.title: Information security risk treatment
nodes.statement: The organisation defines and applies a risk treatment process to select treatment options determine necessary controls and produce a Statement of Applicability.

nodes.title: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
nodes.statement: Information security objectives are established at relevant functions and levels consistent with the policy measurable monitored and updated as appropriate.

nodes.title: Planning of changes
nodes.statement: Changes to the information security management system are carried out in a planned manner.

nodes.title: Resources
nodes.statement: The organisation determines and provides the resources needed for the information security management system.

nodes.title: Competence
nodes.statement: The organisation determines the necessary competence of persons affecting information security performance and ensures they are competent on the basis of education training or experience.

nodes.title: Awareness
nodes.statement: Persons doing work under the organisation's control are aware of the information security policy their contribution to the ISMS and the implications of not conforming.

nodes.title: Communication
nodes.statement: The organisation determines the internal and external communications relevant to the ISMS including what when with whom and how to communicate.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Documented information - general
nodes.statement: The ISMS includes documented information required by the standard and determined by the organisation as necessary for effectiveness.

nodes.title: Creating and updating documented information
nodes.statement: Documented information is appropriately identified described formatted reviewed and approved.

nodes.title: Control of documented information
nodes.statement: Documented information is available where needed and adequately protected including control of distribution access retrieval storage retention and disposition.

nodes.title: Operational planning and control
nodes.statement: The organisation plans implements and controls the processes needed to meet requirements and to implement the actions determined in planning.

nodes.title: Information security risk assessment
nodes.statement: The organisation performs information security risk assessments at planned intervals and when significant changes are proposed or occur and retains documented information on the results.

nodes.title: Information security risk treatment
nodes.statement: The organisation implements the information security risk treatment plan and retains documented information of the results.

nodes.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
nodes.statement: The organisation determines what needs to be monitored and measured the methods to be used and when monitoring measuring analysis and evaluation are performed.

nodes.title: Internal audit - general
nodes.statement: The organisation conducts internal audits at planned intervals to determine whether the ISMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented and maintained.

nodes.title: Internal audit programme
nodes.statement: An audit programme is planned established implemented and maintained including frequency methods responsibilities and reporting.

nodes.title: Management review - general
nodes.statement: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability adequacy and effectiveness.

nodes.title: Management review inputs
nodes.statement: The management review considers the status of prior actions changes in issues and requirements information security performance audit results and opportunities for improvement.

nodes.title: Management review results
nodes.statement: The results of the management review include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the ISMS.

nodes.title: Policies for information security
nodes.statement: Information security policy and topic-specific policies are defined approved by management published and reviewed at planned intervals.

nodes.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
nodes.statement: Rules for acceptable use and procedures for handling information and associated assets are identified documented and implemented.

nodes.title: Return of assets
nodes.statement: Personnel and interested parties return organisational assets on change or termination of employment contract or agreement.

nodes.title: Classification of information
nodes.statement: Information is classified according to confidentiality integrity availability and relevant interested-party requirements.

nodes.title: Labelling of information
nodes.statement: Procedures for labelling information are developed and implemented in accordance with the classification scheme.

nodes.title: Information transfer
nodes.statement: Transfer rules procedures and agreements are in place for all types of transfer facilities.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Access control
nodes.statement: Rules to control physical and logical access to information and associated assets are established and implemented based on business and security requirements.

nodes.title: Identity management
nodes.statement: The full life cycle of identities is managed.

nodes.title: Authentication information
nodes.statement: Allocation and management of authentication information is controlled including advising personnel on appropriate handling.

nodes.title: Access rights
nodes.statement: Access rights to information and associated assets are provisioned reviewed modified and removed in accordance with the access control policy.

nodes.title: Information security in supplier relationships
nodes.statement: Processes and procedures manage the security risks associated with use of supplier products and services.

nodes.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
nodes.statement: Security roles and responsibilities are defined and allocated according to organisational needs.

nodes.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
nodes.statement: Relevant security requirements are established and agreed with each supplier based on the type of relationship.

nodes.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
nodes.statement: Processes and procedures manage security risks associated with the ICT product and service supply chain.

nodes.title: Monitoring review and change management of supplier services
nodes.statement: Changes to supplier services are regularly monitored reviewed evaluated and managed.

nodes.title: Information security for use of cloud services
nodes.statement: Processes for acquisition use management and exit from cloud services are established in accordance with security requirements.

nodes.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
nodes.statement: Incident management is planned and prepared by defining establishing and communicating processes roles and responsibilities.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
nodes.statement: Security events are assessed and a decision is taken on whether they are classified as incidents.

nodes.title: Response to information security incidents
nodes.statement: Security incidents are responded to in accordance with documented procedures.

nodes.title: Learning from information security incidents
nodes.statement: Knowledge gained from incidents is used to strengthen and improve controls.

nodes.title: Collection of evidence
nodes.statement: Procedures for identification collection acquisition and preservation of evidence related to security events are established and implemented.

nodes.title: Information security during disruption
nodes.statement: Plans are in place to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.

nodes.title: Segregation of duties
nodes.statement: Conflicting duties and areas of responsibility are segregated to reduce opportunity for unauthorised or unintentional modification or misuse.

nodes.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
nodes.statement: ICT readiness is planned implemented maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.

nodes.title: Legal statutory regulatory and contractual requirements
nodes.statement: Legal statutory regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security and the approach to meet them are identified documented and kept up to date.

nodes.title: Intellectual property rights
nodes.statement: Appropriate procedures protect intellectual property rights.

nodes.title: Protection of records
nodes.statement: Records are protected from loss destruction falsification unauthorised access and unauthorised release.

nodes.title: Privacy and protection of PII
nodes.statement: Requirements for the preservation of privacy and protection of personally identifiable information are identified and met according to applicable law and contractual requirements.

nodes.title: Independent review of information security
nodes.statement: The approach to managing information security and its implementation are reviewed independently at planned intervals or on significant change.

nodes.title: Compliance with policies rules and standards for information security
nodes.statement: Compliance with the organisation's information security policy topic-specific policies rules and standards is regularly reviewed.

nodes.title: Documented operating procedures
nodes.statement: Operating procedures for information processing facilities are documented and made available to personnel who need them.

nodes.title: Management responsibilities
nodes.statement: Management requires all personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies and procedures.

nodes.title: Contact with authorities
nodes.statement: Appropriate contacts with relevant authorities are established and maintained.

nodes.title: Contact with special interest groups
nodes.statement: Contacts with special interest groups security forums and professional associations are maintained.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Threat intelligence
nodes.statement: Information relating to information security threats is collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.

nodes.title: Information security in project management
nodes.statement: Information security is integrated into project management regardless of project type.

nodes.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
nodes.statement: An inventory of information and other associated assets including owners is developed and maintained.

nodes.title: Screening
nodes.statement: Background verification checks on candidates are carried out prior to joining and on an ongoing basis proportionate to business requirements and perceived risks.

nodes.title: Terms and conditions of employment
nodes.statement: Employment contractual agreements state personnel and organisational responsibilities for information security.

nodes.title: Information security awareness education and training
nodes.statement: Personnel and relevant interested parties receive appropriate awareness education and training and regular updates on policies and procedures relevant to their role.

nodes.title: Disciplinary process
nodes.statement: A formalised and communicated disciplinary process is in place to take action against personnel and other interested parties who have committed a security policy violation.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
nodes.statement: Information security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change of employment are defined enforced and communicated.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
nodes.statement: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organisation's needs are identified documented regularly reviewed and signed.

nodes.title: Remote working
nodes.statement: Security measures are implemented when personnel work remotely to protect information accessed processed or stored outside the organisation's premises.

nodes.title: Information security event reporting
nodes.statement: A mechanism is provided for personnel to report observed or suspected security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.

nodes.title: Physical security perimeters
nodes.statement: Security perimeters are defined and used to protect areas containing information and other associated assets.

nodes.title: Storage media
nodes.statement: Storage media are managed through their life cycle of acquisition use transportation and disposal in accordance with the classification scheme and handling requirements.

nodes.title: Supporting utilities
nodes.statement: Information processing facilities are protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.

nodes.title: Cabling security
nodes.statement: Cables carrying power data or supporting information services are protected from interception interference or damage.

nodes.title: Equipment maintenance
nodes.statement: Equipment is maintained correctly to ensure availability integrity and confidentiality of information.

nodes.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
nodes.statement: Items of equipment containing storage media are verified to ensure sensitive data and licensed software are removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use.

nodes.title: Physical entry
nodes.statement: Secure areas are protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.

nodes.title: Securing offices rooms and facilities
nodes.statement: Physical security for offices rooms and facilities is designed and implemented.

nodes.title: Physical security monitoring
nodes.statement: Premises are continuously monitored for unauthorised physical access.

nodes.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
nodes.statement: Protection against physical and environmental threats such as natural disasters and other intentional or unintentional threats is designed and implemented.

nodes.title: Working in secure areas
nodes.statement: Security measures for working in secure areas are designed and implemented.

nodes.title: Clear desk and clear screen
nodes.statement: Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities are defined and enforced.

nodes.title: Equipment siting and protection
nodes.statement: Equipment is sited securely and protected.

nodes.title: Security of assets off-premises
nodes.statement: Off-site assets are protected.

nodes.title: User endpoint devices
nodes.statement: Information stored on processed by or accessible via user endpoint devices is protected.

nodes.title: Information deletion
nodes.statement: Information stored in information systems devices or other storage media is deleted when no longer required.

nodes.title: Data masking
nodes.statement: Data masking is used in accordance with the access control policy and other related policies and business requirements taking applicable legislation into consideration.

nodes.title: Data leakage prevention
nodes.statement: Data leakage prevention measures are applied to systems networks and other devices that process store or transmit sensitive information.

nodes.title: Information backup
nodes.statement: Backup copies of information software and systems are maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed backup policy.

nodes.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
nodes.statement: Information processing facilities are implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements.

nodes.title: Logging
nodes.statement: Logs that record activities exceptions faults and other relevant events are produced stored protected and analysed.

nodes.title: Monitoring activities
nodes.statement: Networks systems and applications are monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions are taken to evaluate potential security incidents.

nodes.title: Clock synchronization
nodes.statement: The clocks of information processing systems are synchronised to approved time sources.

nodes.title: Use of privileged utility programs
nodes.statement: The use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls is restricted and tightly controlled.

nodes.title: Installation of software on operational systems
nodes.statement: Procedures and measures are implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems.

nodes.title: Privileged access rights
nodes.statement: The allocation and use of privileged access rights is restricted and managed.

nodes.title: Networks security
nodes.statement: Networks and network devices are secured managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

nodes.title: Security of network services
nodes.statement: Security mechanisms service levels and service requirements of network services are identified implemented and monitored.

nodes.title: Segregation of networks
nodes.statement: Groups of information services users and information systems are segregated in the organisation's networks.

nodes.title: Web filtering
nodes.statement: Access to external websites is managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.

nodes.title: Use of cryptography
nodes.statement: Rules for the effective use of cryptography including cryptographic key management are defined and implemented.

nodes.title: Secure development life cycle
nodes.statement: Rules for the secure development of software and systems are established and applied.

nodes.title: Application security requirements
nodes.statement: Information security requirements are identified specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.

nodes.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
nodes.statement: Principles for engineering secure systems are established documented maintained and applied to information system development activities.

nodes.title: Secure coding
nodes.statement: Secure coding principles are applied to software development.

nodes.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
nodes.statement: Security testing processes are defined and implemented in the development life cycle.

nodes.title: Information access restriction
nodes.statement: Access to information and other associated assets is restricted in accordance with the established access control policy.

nodes.title: Outsourced development
nodes.statement: The organisation directs monitors and reviews the activities related to outsourced system development.

nodes.title: Separation of development test and production environments
nodes.statement: Development testing and production environments are separated and secured.

nodes.title: Change management
nodes.statement: Changes to information processing facilities and information systems are subject to change management procedures.

nodes.title: Test information
nodes.statement: Test information is appropriately selected protected and managed.

nodes.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
nodes.statement: Audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems are planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.

nodes.title: Access to source code
nodes.statement: Read and write access to source code development tools and software libraries is appropriately managed.

nodes.title: Secure authentication
nodes.statement: Secure authentication technologies and procedures are implemented based on information access restrictions and the access control policy.

nodes.title: Capacity management
nodes.statement: The use of resources is monitored and adjusted in line with current and expected capacity requirements.

nodes.title: Protection against malware
nodes.statement: Protection against malware is implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.

nodes.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
nodes.statement: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use is obtained exposure to such vulnerabilities is evaluated and appropriate measures are taken.

nodes.title: Configuration management
nodes.statement: Configurations including security configurations of hardware software services and networks are established documented implemented monitored and reviewed.

nodes.title: Continual improvement
nodes.statement: The organisation continually improves the suitability adequacy and effectiveness of the AI management system.

nodes.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
nodes.statement: When a nonconformity occurs the organisation reacts to it evaluates the need for action to eliminate its causes implements action and reviews effectiveness.

nodes.statement: The AI management system includes documented information required by the standard and determined by the organisation as necessary for effectiveness.

nodes.title: Creating and updating documented information
nodes.statement: Documented information is appropriately identified described formatted reviewed and approved.

nodes.title: Control of documented information
nodes.statement: Documented information is available where needed and adequately protected including control of distribution access retrieval storage retention and disposition.

nodes.title: Operational planning and control
nodes.statement: The organisation plans implements and controls the processes needed to meet requirements and to implement the actions determined in planning.

nodes.title: AI risk assessment
nodes.statement: The organisation performs AI risk assessments at planned intervals and when significant changes are proposed or occur and retains documented information on the results.

nodes.title: AI risk treatment
nodes.statement: The organisation implements the AI risk treatment plan and retains documented information of the results.

nodes.title: AI system impact assessment
nodes.statement: The organisation performs AI system impact assessments at planned intervals and retains documented information on the results.

nodes.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
nodes.statement: The organisation determines what needs to be monitored and measured the methods to be used and when monitoring measuring analysis and evaluation are performed.

nodes.title: Internal audit - general
nodes.statement: The organisation conducts internal audits at planned intervals to determine whether the AI management system conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented and maintained.

nodes.title: Internal audit programme
nodes.statement: An audit programme is planned established implemented and maintained including frequency methods responsibilities and reporting.

nodes.title: Management review - general
nodes.statement: Top management reviews the AI management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability adequacy and effectiveness.

nodes.title: Management review inputs
nodes.statement: The management review considers the status of prior actions changes in issues and requirements AI performance audit results and opportunities for improvement.

nodes.title: Management review results
nodes.statement: The results of the management review include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AI management system.

nodes.title: Allocating responsibilities
nodes.statement: Responsibilities are allocated between the organisation and third parties across the AI system life cycle.

nodes.title: Suppliers
nodes.statement: Requirements are established for suppliers of AI systems components or services and supplier conformance is assessed.

nodes.title: Customers
nodes.statement: The organisation's responsibilities to customers of its AI systems are defined including information provided to them.

nodes.title: AI policy
nodes.statement: The organisation documents an AI policy that is approved by management and establishes the organisation's intentions and direction for responsible development and use of AI.

nodes.title: Alignment with other organizational policies
nodes.statement: The AI policy is aligned with other organisational policies such as information security privacy quality and safety so that requirements do not conflict.

nodes.title: Review of the AI policy
nodes.statement: The AI policy is reviewed at planned intervals or when significant changes occur to ensure continuing suitability adequacy and effectiveness.

nodes.title: AI roles and responsibilities
nodes.statement: Roles and responsibilities for AI are defined and allocated across the organisation including accountability for AI system outcomes.

nodes.title: Reporting of concerns
nodes.statement: A mechanism is provided for personnel and other interested parties to report concerns about the organisation's AI systems.

nodes.title: Resource documentation
nodes.statement: The organisation identifies and documents the resources required for activities at each AI system life cycle stage.

nodes.title: Data resources
nodes.statement: Data resources used for AI systems are documented including their characteristics and intended role.

nodes.title: Tooling resources
nodes.statement: Tooling resources used in the development and operation of AI systems are documented.

nodes.title: System and computing resources
nodes.statement: System and computing resources used for AI systems are documented including infrastructure needed across the life cycle.

nodes.title: Human resources
nodes.statement: Human resources and the competences required for AI activities are documented including specialist skills.

nodes.title: AI system impact assessment process
nodes.statement: A process is established to assess the potential consequences of AI systems for individuals groups and society throughout the life cycle.

nodes.title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
nodes.statement: The results of AI system impact assessments are documented and retained.

nodes.title: Assessing AI system impact on individuals and groups of individuals
nodes.statement: The potential impacts of the AI system on individuals and groups of individuals are assessed including impacts on health safety and fundamental rights.

nodes.title: Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
nodes.statement: The potential broader societal impacts of AI systems are assessed including environmental economic and social effects.

nodes.title: Objectives for responsible development of AI system
nodes.statement: Objectives for the responsible development of AI systems are defined and documented.

nodes.title: Processes for responsible design and development of AI systems
nodes.statement: Processes for the responsible design and development of AI systems are defined and implemented.

nodes.title: AI system requirements and specification
nodes.statement: Requirements for the AI system are specified including functional performance and trustworthiness requirements.

nodes.title: Documentation of AI system design and development
nodes.statement: The design and development of the AI system is documented including design decisions and their rationale.

nodes.title: AI system verification and validation
nodes.statement: Verification and validation measures for the AI system are defined and performed and the results documented.

nodes.title: AI system deployment
nodes.statement: A deployment plan is defined and requirements are met before the AI system is deployed into operational use.

nodes.title: AI system operation and monitoring
nodes.statement: The AI system is operated and monitored in accordance with defined requirements including ongoing performance monitoring after deployment.

nodes.title: AI system technical documentation
nodes.statement: Technical documentation for the AI system is produced and maintained for relevant interested parties.

nodes.title: AI system recording of event logs
nodes.statement: The AI system automatically records event logs during its operation and logs are retained for a defined period.

nodes.title: Data for development and enhancement of AI system
nodes.statement: The organisation defines and documents the data management process for data used to develop and enhance AI systems.

nodes.title: Acquisition of data
nodes.statement: Data acquired for AI systems is obtained in accordance with defined requirements including legal and contractual constraints.

nodes.title: Quality of data for AI systems
nodes.statement: The quality of data used in AI systems is defined assessed and maintained including relevance representativeness and accuracy.

nodes.title: Data provenance
nodes.statement: The provenance of data used in AI systems is recorded and maintained including origin and transformations applied.

nodes.title: Data preparation
nodes.statement: Data preparation methods applied to data used in AI systems are defined and documented.

nodes.title: System documentation and information for users
nodes.statement: Documentation is provided to users of the AI system so they can understand its capabilities limitations and appropriate use.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: External reporting
nodes.statement: A capability is provided for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system externally.

nodes.title: Communication of incidents
nodes.statement: A process is defined for communicating AI system incidents to relevant interested parties.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Information for interested parties
nodes.statement: Information about the AI system is made available to interested parties as appropriate to their role and needs.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
nodes.statement: Processes for the responsible use of AI systems are defined and implemented.

nodes.title: Objectives for responsible use of AI system
nodes.statement: Objectives for the responsible use of the AI system are defined and documented.

nodes.title: Intended use of the AI system
nodes.statement: The intended use of the AI system is defined and the system is used in accordance with that intended use and its documented limitations.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
nodes.statement: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

nodes.title: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
nodes.statement: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.

nodes.title: Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization’s risk tolerance.
nodes.statement: Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization’s risk tolerance.

nodes.title: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
nodes.statement: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.

nodes.title: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined, including determining the frequency of
nodes.statement: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.

nodes.title: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
nodes.statement: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.

nodes.title: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization’s trustworthiness.
nodes.statement: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization’s trustworthiness.

nodes.title: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.
nodes.statement: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

nodes.title: The organization’s personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.
nodes.statement: The organization’s personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.

nodes.title: Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.
nodes.statement: Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.

nodes.title: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and ba
nodes.statement: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).

nodes.title: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
nodes.statement: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.

nodes.title: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative
nodes.statement: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.

nodes.title: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.
nodes.statement: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.

nodes.title: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
nodes.statement: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.

nodes.title: Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the poten
nodes.statement: Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.

nodes.statement: Mechanisms are established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.

nodes.statement: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.

nodes.title: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third- party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.
nodes.statement: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third- party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.

nodes.title: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
nodes.statement: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.

nodes.title: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.
nodes.statement: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.

nodes.title: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or acce
nodes.statement: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

nodes.title: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.
nodes.statement: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.

nodes.title: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account – along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods – to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.
nodes.statement: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account – along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods – to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.

nodes.title: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.
nodes.statement: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.

nodes.title: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
nodes.statement: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.

nodes.title: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with inte
nodes.statement: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.

nodes.title: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.
nodes.statement: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.

nodes.title: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
nodes.statement: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.

nodes.title: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incid
nodes.statement: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.

nodes.title: Measurable activities for continual improvements are integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.
nodes.statement: Measurable activities for continual improvements are integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.

nodes.title: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented
nodes.statement: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented.

nodes.title: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considera
nodes.statement: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: the specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; and related TEVV and system metrics.

concepts.label: Information for users and interested parties

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, and their participation is docu
nodes.statement: Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, and their participation is documented. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are prioritized.

nodes.title: The organization’s mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented
nodes.statement: The organization’s mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented

nodes.title: The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or – in the case of assessing existing AI systems – re-evaluated.
nodes.statement: The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or – in the case of assessing existing AI systems – re-evaluated.

nodes.title: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.
nodes.statement: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.

nodes.title: System requirements (e.g., “the system shall respect the privacy of its users”) are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account
nodes.statement: System requirements (e.g., “the system shall respect the privacy of its users”) are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.

nodes.title: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).
nodes.statement: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).

nodes.statement: Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making decisions and taking subsequent actions

nodes.statement: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness, and construct validation.

nodes.title: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
nodes.statement: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.

nodes.statement: Potential costs, including non- monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness – as connected to organizational risk tolerance – are examined and documented

nodes.statement: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system’s capability, established context, and AI system categorization.

nodes.statement: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness – and relevant technical standards and certifications – are defined, assessed, and documented.

nodes.title: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.
nodes.statement: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.

nodes.statement: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components – including the use of third-party data or software – are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third party’s intellectual property or other rights.

nodes.title: Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.
nodes.statement: Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.

nodes.statement: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data are identified and documented.

nodes.statement: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.

nodes.statement: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls are regularly assessed and updated, including reports of errors and potential impacts on affected communities.

nodes.statement: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.

nodes.statement: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.

nodes.statement: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
